Denial of cough, sore throat, ear pain aligns with respective gold ROS negatives.
Diffuse myalgias corresponds to body/muscle aches in gold HPI.
Nausea and poor PO intake map to nausea and drinking less than normal in the gold HPI (hpi-001 and hpi-002).

Denies neck stiffness matches gold ROS.

Denies rash matches gold ROS.
Denies joint swelling is part of gold ROS-009 (though gold also notes concurrent back pain).
No urinary symptoms is consistent with no dysuria or frequency.

Malaria prophylaxis, likely daily, with unknown agent corresponds to daily malaria prevention with unknown medication in gold.
Gold does not mention the patient taking an additional prophylaxis tablet; this is new information without direct support or conflict.
Chronic back pain under physiotherapy is consistent with gold PMH (back pain under physiotherapy; muscular/posture).
Ceraset vs Cerazette is a spelling discrepancy but clearly the same medication.
Gold confirms OTC paracetamol use but does not specify that doses are ‘at recommended doses’; that qualifier is an added detail.
Gold confirms OTC ibuprofen use but does not state dosing details; ‘at recommended doses’ is additional.
Generated fact lists pollen allergy causing hay fever, while gold explicitly states nil allergies; this directly conflicts.
Gold only states that father had MI at 68; the detail that he died of MI is additional but not contradictory.

Non-smoker status matches gold.

Moderate exercise a few times/week is consistent with moderate physical exercise.
Vaccinations up to date including Hep B is consistent with being UTD with Hep B in gold social history.
Describes an acute febrile illness for 7 days with systemic symptoms and no clear source, which is consistent with pyrexia of unknown origin impression in gold.
Concern for malaria after Vietnam travel aligns with gold’s ‘need to exclude malaria’; mention of other travel-associated infections is an addition but not contradictory.
Reduced PO intake leading to dehydration risk is a reasonable clinical interpretation of drinking less than normal; this is an extrapolation but consistent with the gold data.
Chronic low back pain stable and under physiotherapy is aligned with gold PMH description.
Urgent in-person clinic exam today is equivalent to face-to-face GP appointment today; added location and purpose are extra detail.

Supported by gold plan-002 regarding thick and thin films for malaria and inflammatory markers, but gold specifies CRP/ESR, while generated refers only to ‘inflammatory markers and baseline bloods’ more generally.
